_comment: USD per 1,000,000 tokens. Keys under 'models' are matched against the
transcript's message.model by LONGEST PREFIX, so both 'claude-haiku-4-5'
and 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' resolve to the same entry.
Derived rates follow Anthropic's standard multipliers on base input:
cache_read = 0.1x, cache_write_5m = 1.25x, cache_write_1h = 2x.
A model entry may carry rate VARIANTS, which replace the base five for
one request. Which variant applies is read off that request's own usage
block, never guessed from the model name:
speed.fast    -- usage.speed == 'fast', what /fast turns on. Applies
across the full context window.
long_context  -- present on every model whose window exceeds 200K.
A request whose total input passes 'threshold' is
marked (1m) in the ledger. With only a threshold the
marker prices at BASE rates -- deliberate, not lazy:
Claude 4.6+ include the 1M window at standard pricing
('a 900k-token request is billed at the same per-token
rate as a 9k-token request'), and Claude Code's own
per-project costUSD for 'claude-opus-5[1m]' usage
reconstructs to exactly standard rates. Add the five
rate keys to a block and they take over above the
threshold -- as on sonnet-4-5, whose retired 1M beta
really did bill >200K requests at 2x input / 1.5x
output. A block with SOME rate keys but not all five
prices as unknown rather than guessing the gaps.
'modifiers' scale every category and stack on top of whichever variant
applied. A value we have no factor for prices as unknown rather than
quietly standard.
Source: platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing. Verified 2026-08-25.
Sonnet 5's $2/$10 launch pricing is now its standard price -- the rise to
$3/$15 scheduled for 2026-09-01 was cancelled.
